chunks: What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said:
"For defecation, wiping with stones suffices; but for urine, nothing suffices except water."

As for the report narrated by Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir al-Qasabani, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: I prayed, then remembered that I had not washed my penis after I had prayed; should I repeat? He said: "No."

Its meaning is that it is not obligatory for him to repeat the wudu (ablution); rather, what is obligatory for him is to repeat the washing of the area. There is nothing in the report stating that repeating the salat (prayer) is not obligatory for him, and what indicates this interpretation is what has preceded of the reports, and it makes it even clearer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); the prayer whose repetition is discussed
key_terms.الْأَحْجَارِ: stones; the material used for dry cleansing after defecation
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine; the impurity for which only water suffices
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: feces; the excretion for which wiping with stones is said to suffice
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water; the required means of purification from urine
key_terms.الْمَسْحُ: wiping; the act of cleansing with stones
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution); the ritual ablution discussed in relation to repetition
key_terms.غَسْلِ الْمَوْضِعِ: washing the area; the cleansing that remains obligatory

ai.seo_question: Does wiping suffice after relieving oneself, and is water required after urination in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage presents a legal ruling on purification after relieving oneself: wiping with stones suffices for feces, while urine requires water. It also discusses a report about forgetting to wash after urination, clarifying that the report negates repeating wudu (ablution), not necessarily repeating the salat (prayer), based on other narrations.
